---
title: Measles wastewater surveillance with epiworldR
format: gfm
---

This project models measles in a synthetic Salt Lake County population with
community and school contact layers. It compares no surveillance-triggered
intervention with case and wastewater triggers. The model is an exploratory
simulation, not an estimate of an actual outbreak.

## Run the model

Install `epiworldR` from the `v1-layers` commit used here and install
`multigroup.vaccine`, `measles`, `data.table`, and `remotes`:

```r
remotes::install_github("UofUEpiBio/epiworldR@2f1a5acc7835c44908fab53261d879afc4335e51")
```

From the repository root, run `Rscript analysis/run-layered-example.R` for a
single seeded comparison or `Rscript analysis/run-scenarios.R` for the larger
simulation study. Run `Rscript -e 'tinytest::run_test_dir("tests")'` to check
the code. A UTF-8 locale may be required to read the Census files.

## Population and contacts

The 2025 county age distribution comes from Census data supplied by
`multigroup.vaccine`. School assignments use Utah school records and 2023 ACS
district residential populations, as documented in [data/utah](data/utah/README.md).
These are approximate assignments, not observed enrollment; five-year age
bands are used as proxies for school levels. Every agent participates in the
community layer, and assigned students also participate in one school group.
School MMR coverage is taken from the school data; `prop_vaccinated` sets
coverage for other agents. A vaccinated agent receives susceptibility
reduction `vax_efficacy`.

Community contacts use the household, work and other Epistorm-Mix matrices.
The school layer uses within-school mixing. Simulation scaling can leave small
school groups unable to achieve their target number of contacts. The setup
calibrates both layers against simulated transmission in a fully susceptible
population, including seeded cases with no secondary infections.

## Measles and surveillance

The disease stages are susceptible, latent, prodromal, rash, hospitalized and
recovered. Latent, prodromal and rash durations are independent lognormal draws
with means and standard deviations in days, rounded to whole days with a
minimum of one. Defaults are 10 (SD 2.5), 4 (SD 1.7), and 4 (SD 1),
respectively. Lessler et al. estimate exposure to first symptoms, so applying
that shape and SD to exposure to infectiousness is an approximation; the
prodromal SD comes from a Hagelloch data fit and the rash SD is an assumption.
See [Lessler et al. (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1473-3099(09)70069-6)
and the [measles parameter documentation](https://uofuepibio.github.io/measles/articles/parameters.html).

The layer engine currently accepts only zero or full stage contact weights.
To approximate reduced rash contact, a fraction of rash cases is selected for
isolation through a global event. Isolation takes effect after the event and
entry into the isolated stage draws a new rash duration. This is an approximation
and does not precisely preserve each individual's rash duration or partial
contacts. Hospitalization competes with rash recovery. The wastewater model
uses the existing shedding curve and assumes that the whole simulated
population contributes to the catchment. Detection triggers a reduction in
school contacts; community contacts remain unchanged.

## Simulation results

The results below use 400 paired simulations per scenario, a population of
10,000 agents, one initial infection, and 365 days of follow-up. The two
coverage scenarios set vaccination among non-students to 0% and 85%; school
coverage remains school-specific in both scenarios. The wastewater threshold
is calibrated separately for each coverage scenario against the case trigger.
Agent and vaccination assignments are held fixed across runs; epidemic seeds
run from 1001 to 1400. An outbreak is a baseline simulation with at least 50
infections. The outcome
summaries below are conditional on those baseline outbreaks; the outbreak
percentage uses all simulations. Scenario pairs share their random seed.

```{r}
#| include: false
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
source("R/parameters.R")
results <- readRDS("analysis/results.rds")
tab <- function(x, digits = 1) knitr::kable(as.data.frame(x), digits = digits)
```

### Calibration and outbreak frequency

The simulated reproduction number is estimated in a fully susceptible
population. The intervention estimate reduces school contacts only; both
estimates are subject to Monte Carlo variation. The wastewater threshold is
chosen so the median number of prodromal cases at sample collection matches
the median number of rash cases at the clinical report that crosses the case
threshold. Calibration uses baseline runs in which the case trigger fires;
wastewater non-detections count as missed outbreaks.

```{r}
#| echo: false
calibration <- rbindlist(lapply(names(results), function(coverage) {
  x <- results[[coverage]]
  data.table(nonstudent_coverage = paste0(100 * as.numeric(coverage), "%"),
             simulated_R0 = x$R0_sim, intervention_R = x$R_int,
             wastewater_threshold = x$calibration$threshold,
             baseline_outbreak_pct = x$summary[scenario == "baseline", pct_outbreak])
}))
tab(calibration, 2)
```

### Scenario comparison

Infections averted compare each scenario with its paired baseline. Trigger
day and lead time are medians among runs for which they are defined. Positive
lead means the wastewater trigger preceded the case trigger. The baseline
row's trigger-related quantities are not applicable.

```{r}
#| echo: false
summary_table <- rbindlist(lapply(names(results), function(coverage) {
  x <- copy(results[[coverage]]$summary)
  x[, nonstudent_coverage := paste0(100 * as.numeric(coverage), "%")]
  x[scenario == "baseline", lead_median := NA_real_]
  x[, .(nonstudent_coverage, scenario, nsims, pct_trigger, trigger_day,
        final_size, final_q25, final_q75, averted, lead_median)]
}))
tab(summary_table, 1)
```

The curves show the mean across all simulations, including introductions
that do not reach the outbreak threshold; they are not conditional on an
outbreak.

```{r}
#| label: fig-layered-curves
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false
curves <- rbindlist(lapply(results, `[[`, "curves"))
curves[, coverage := paste0(100 * as.numeric(coverage), "% non-student coverage")]
ggplot(curves, aes(day, new_inf, color = scenario)) +
  geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ coverage, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Simulation day", y = "Mean new infections", color = "Scenario") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Sensitivity analyses

The wastewater threshold is held at its reference value within each coverage
scenario. The tables are conditional on baseline outbreaks. Laboratory delay
and sampling-frequency rows report wastewater-triggered runs; case-detection
rows report case-triggered runs. Lead times compare each run with its paired
reference trigger.

```{r}
#| echo: false
sensitivity <- function(field, variable) {
  rbindlist(lapply(names(results), function(coverage) {
    x <- copy(results[[coverage]][[field]])
    x[, nonstudent_coverage := paste0(100 * as.numeric(coverage), "%")]
    x[, c("nonstudent_coverage", variable, "nsims", "pct_trigger", "trigger_day",
          "final_size", "averted", "lead_median"), with = FALSE]
  }))
}
```

**Wastewater laboratory delay (days)**

```{r}
#| echo: false
tab(sensitivity("lab_delay", "ww_lab_delay"))
```

**Wastewater sampling frequency (days per week)**

```{r}
#| echo: false
tab(sensitivity("sampling", "samples_per_week"))
```

**Case detection probability**

```{r}
#| echo: false
tab(sensitivity("report_prob", "case_report_prob"))
```

## Parameters and sources

The table gives the defaults for the current model; wastewater thresholds
shown above are calibrated separately for each coverage scenario.

```{r}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(format_ww_parameters(ww_parameters()), escape = FALSE)
```

## Reproducibility and limitations

The saved aggregate results are in [analysis/results.rds](analysis/results.rds).
Earlier reports and parameters are available in Git history.
See [data/parameters.csv](data/parameters.csv) for the parameter table and
sources, and [data/epistorm](data/epistorm/README.md) for contact matrices.
These scenarios use assumptions about school membership, immunity, shedding,
contact rates and response behavior. They do not constitute forecasts or
validate wastewater sensitivity against observed Salt Lake County outbreaks.

Reusable setup accepts explicit population counts, school records, school
weights, and contact matrices. `salt_lake_inputs()` is the current application
adapter; other locations supply the same input structure to `build_setup()`.
Setup functions consume the caller's R RNG stream. Execution scripts initialize
the stream and reset it at paired-replicate boundaries. The results above were
generated before this seed-ownership refactor, with the former fixed setup
seeds; they have not been regenerated for new caller-selected populations.
